nfdc2208e174.s: Strontium-90 in fallout from nuclear weapons testing belongs to which category of radioactive pollution?
nfdc2208e174.x: Fallout from weapons tests (Sr-90) is a man-made nuclear source; cosmic rays, radon and potassium-40 are natural.

nd5a53c93f4b.s: As the temperature of water rises, its capacity to hold dissolved oxygen:
nd5a53c93f4b.x: Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen, which is why thermal pollution stresses aquatic life.

n2d23e120a97.s: Which of the following is an effect of prolonged exposure to noise?
n2d23e120a97.x: Prolonged noise exposure constricts blood vessels, causes digestive spasms and impairs (not improves) night vision.

nbf428b0a0ef.s: Protecting and improving the natural environment is a fundamental duty of citizens under which Article?
nbf428b0a0ef.x: Article 51A(g) is the citizen's fundamental duty; Article 48A is a separate Directive Principle for the State.

n13b45ce1bd5.s: Which of the following is a conventional pollution-control method, not an alternative technology?
n13b45ce1bd5.x: Incineration is a conventional method; green technology, bioremediation and carbon capture and storage are the alternatives (APPSC-G2 2025 trap).

n151fc1bafd7.s: Which of the following pairs (substance – behaviour in marine food chains) is correctly matched?
n151fc1bafd7.x: DDT and mercury biomagnify through marine food chains; dissolved oxygen is not a pollutant and does not biomagnify.

ndisaster-management-7-6.s: Who acts as the Incident Commander during an off-site nuclear emergency?
ndisaster-management-7-6.x: The District Collector is the Incident Commander in an off-site emergency, under NDMA's 2009 nuclear and radiological guidelines.

n3a33ace913e.s: Environmental Compensation under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 follows which principle?
n3a33ace913e.x: Environmental Compensation follows the polluter-pays principle, not the precautionary principle.

n8d52a1c8d5e.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, paper, plastics and metals go into which bin?
n8d52a1c8d5e.x: Paper, plastics and metals go in the dry bin; wet waste covers food scraps, peels and garden waste.

nc6cfd145881.s: Under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026, unmet targets may be carried forward for up to:
nc6cfd145881.x: The 2026 amendment allows unmet targets to be carried forward for up to three years, not five.

n5f273a89414.s: Microbeads are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules in which products?
n5f273a89414.x: The PWM Rules ban microbeads in cosmetics; separately, an FSSAI study found microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.

n17aad19669e.s: How many Municipal Corporations does Andhra Pradesh have?
n17aad19669e.x: AP's urban set-up has 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.

naa8fdcdf9df.s: The Indore method of composting is:
o: Anaerobic pits with alternate layers of solid waste and night soil
Aerobic composting with the waste turned at intervals
naa8fdcdf9df.x: The Indore method is aerobic composting with turning at intervals; anaerobic pits with layers of MSW and night soil are the Bangalore method.

n913ac9bf010.s: In hazardous-waste disposal, which option is treated as the last resort?
n913ac9bf010.x: Landfill is the last resort; APPCB prefers co-processing as fuel in cement plants and waste exchange between industries.

nenvironment-26-4.s: Vermicompost is compost produced with the help of:
nenvironment-26-4.x: Vermicompost is made by earthworms, which makes vermicomposting a biological method of composting.

nenvironment-40-8.s: Hydrogen is regarded as a clean fuel because hydrogen fuel cells emit only:
nenvironment-40-8.x: Hydrogen fuel cells emit only water vapour, which is why hydrogen is considered a clean fuel.

n72cd477bcac.s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, the recycled-content target for rigid plastics rises from 2025-26 as:
n72cd477bcac.x: Rigid plastics go from 30% to 60%; flexible single-layer from 10% to 20%; multi-layered from 5% to 10%.

n41f395e3d6b.s: How many colour categories do the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 use?
n41f395e3d6b.x: The 2016 Rules use four colour categories with barcoding and GPS tracking; ten categories belonged to the 1998 Rules.

n26f9f6b9a81.s: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, contaminated recyclable plastics such as IV sets and catheters go into which category?
n26f9f6b9a81.x: Contaminated recyclable plastics go into Red; Yellow is for anatomical waste and expired medicines.

n12b9b57aae3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INC-5.2 plastics treaty meeting?
o: It was held in Geneva in August 2025
It ended with adoption of a final treaty text
Production caps and finance were major sticking points
n12b9b57aae3.x: INC-5.2 ended without agreement because of disputes over production caps, chemicals of concern and finance; no treaty text was adopted.

n1d8d9276973.s: The E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022 came into force on:
n1d8d9276973.x: The Rules were notified in November 2022 and came into force on 1 April 2023; their 106 EEE items include solar PV waste.

n34a97bb3bf6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about solid waste in India?
o: Urban areas account for only about 20% of all waste generated
About 60% of waste comes from urban areas
n34a97bb3bf6.x: About 60% of India's waste comes from urban areas, not 20%; SBM-U processing rose from 16% (2014) to 82% (2026).

n0293b08ecad.s: The Re Sustainability MoU in Andhra Pradesh for e-waste collection and material recovery facilities covers how many ULBs?
n0293b08ecad.x: The Re Sustainability MoU covers all 123 ULBs; the 30-ULB figure relates to the ITC MoU.

n26751e623ea.s: APPCB has permitted how many cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste?
n26751e623ea.x: APPCB permitted 12 cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste.

nc2245f083a9.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2022, which Andhra Pradesh city was named 'Top Impact Creator' (million-plus)?
nc2245f083a9.x: Visakhapatnam was 'Top Impact Creator'; Tirupati came first in 'Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar' (APPSC-G1 2022).

nenvironment-39-3.s: Increased plant growth because higher atmospheric CO2 raises the rate of photosynthesis is called:
nenvironment-39-3.x: Carbon fertilisation is faster plant growth driven by extra CO2 speeding up photosynthesis.

nb62b64d8619.s: The process of capturing CO2 from industrial processes and storing it so that it does not enter the atmosphere is called:
nb62b64d8619.x: This is carbon sequestration (APPSC-GS 2024 key). Carbon leakage is emissions moving abroad; offsetting uses credits to balance emissions.

nenvironment-39-1.s: Carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems is called:
nenvironment-39-1.x: Blue carbon is carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems; geological storage uses coal seams, depleted reservoirs and saline formations.

n89dcff997c7.s: The UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) starts on:
n89dcff997c7.x: The UK CBAM starts on 1 January 2027; the EU CBAM's definitive phase began on 1 January 2026.

new.s: The major primary cause of soil pollution is:
new.x: Soil pollution is mainly from chemical fertilisers and pesticides; sewage is for water, industry for air, construction for noise.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (pollution type – major cause) is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: Hot cooling water from thermal and nuclear plants causes thermal pollution; soil pollution comes mainly from fertilisers and pesticides.

new.s: Itai-itai disease is caused by which heavy metal?
new.x: Cadmium causes itai-itai; mercury causes Minamata disease.

new.s: Cadmium pollution of soil comes mainly from:
o: Phosphate fertilisers, batteries and mining effluent
new.x: Cadmium comes from phosphate fertilisers, batteries and mining effluent; mercury from chlor-alkali effluent, chromates from tanneries.

new.s: Chromates in soil are mainly released by which industry?
new.x: Chromates come from tanneries; mercury comes from chlor-alkali effluent.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a soil-pollution control measure (APPSC 2019 trap)?
new.x: Biofertilisers, IPM and crop rotation control soil pollution; watersheds are NOT a soil-pollution control.

new.s: Landfill leachate is a cause of which type of pollution, listed among its human causes?
new.x: Human causes of soil pollution include pesticides, NPK, heavy metals, landfill leachate, e-waste, coal ash and mining.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about soil pollution:
1. Floods and acid rain are natural causes of soil pollution.
2. The Contaminated Sites Rules follow the Polluter Pays principle.
3. The Contaminated Sites Rules cover radioactive waste sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Floods, acid rain and weathered rock are natural causes, and the Rules follow Polluter Pays; but radioactive waste is exempt from them.

new.s: Under the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules, what share of the fund does the Centre keep?
new.x: Under the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules, the Centre keeps 25%.

new.s: The use of plants to take up toxic substances such as heavy metals from soil and water is called:
new.x: Phytoremediation uses plants; hyperaccumulator plants store very high levels of heavy metals.

new.s: Mycoremediation uses which agents to break down or absorb pollutants?
o: Fungi such as the oyster mushroom
new.x: Mycoremediation uses fungi (e.g. oyster mushroom, Pleurotus) to break down oil, DDT and heavy metals.

new.s: Adding pollutant-degrading microbes to a contaminated site is called:
new.x: Bioaugmentation adds pollutant-degrading microbes; biostimulation only adds nutrients to boost native microbes.

new.s: Permanent hearing loss can result from prolonged exposure to sound above:
new.x: Above 85 dB can cause permanent hearing loss; WHO's safe indoor level is below 30 dB.

new.s: Which pair (sound – approximate level) is correctly matched?
new.x: Heavy traffic is about 90 dB; conversation about 60 dB, rustling leaves about 20 dB, rocket engine about 180 dB.

new.s: Under the Noise Rules, 2000, the day-time ambient noise limit for an industrial area is:
new.x: Industrial areas: 75 dB(A) by day and 70 by night; residential 55/45; silence 50/40.

new.s: For the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, 'day time' means:
new.x: Day time under the Noise Rules runs from 6 am to 10 pm.

new.s: Hertz is the unit of which property of sound?
new.x: Hertz measures frequency; noise intensity is measured in decibels.

new.s: CPCB's NANMN has 70 stations across how many metro cities?
new.x: The National Ambient Noise Monitoring Network has 70 stations in 7 metros.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a noise-control measure?
new.x: Silencers, noise barriers and green belts control noise; cooling towers control thermal pollution.

new.s: Green mufflers consist of how many rows of trees or shrubs planted along roads?
new.x: Green mufflers are 4–5 rows of trees or shrubs along roads that absorb noise, gases and dust.

new.s: Thermal pollution of water can be controlled by using:
new.x: Cooling towers, cooling ponds, recirculation and regulated discharge temperature control thermal pollution.

new.s: Thermal pollution of water bodies is caused by hot coolant water from:
new.x: Hot coolant water from thermal and nuclear plants and industries changes water temperature.

new.s: The secretariat of SACEP (1982) is located at:
new.x: SACEP was set up in 1982 with its secretariat in Colombo; it has 8 members including India.

new.s: The GloLitter Partnerships is funded by:
new.x: GloLitter (IMO and FAO, 2019) is funded by Norway; India is a partner.

new.s: Hypoxic waters caused by nutrient runoff, as in the Gulf of Mexico, are called:
new.x: Dead zones are hypoxic waters from nutrient runoff; ghost nets are abandoned fishing gear.

new.s: The Ballast Water Management Convention mainly addresses:
new.x: The IMO Ballast Water Convention (in force 2017) targets invasive species.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about MARPOL 73/78:
1. It is administered by the IMO.
2. It has six Annexes.
3. It permits dumping of plastics at sea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: MARPOL is an IMO convention with 6 Annexes and it bans plastic dumping at sea, so statement 3 is wrong.

new.s: Which radioactive element in building materials was asked in APPSC 2019?
new.x: Thorium in building materials (APPSC 2019); radon also comes from granite.

new.s: The sievert and the rem are units of:
new.x: Sievert and rem measure biological dose; becquerel/curie measure activity; gray/rad measure absorbed dose.

new.s: The rad is a unit of:
new.x: Rad (like gray) measures absorbed dose; it is NOT a unit of activity, which is measured in becquerel and curie.

new.s: Which of the following is a medical contributor to radioactive pollution?
new.x: I-125, P-32, C-14 and X-rays are medical sources; K-40, radon-222 and Th-232 are natural.

new.s: Radon is produced in soil by the decay of:
new.x: Radon is a colourless, odourless noble gas from radium decay in soil.

new.s: In which year did NDMA issue its National Guidelines on Management of Nuclear and Radiological Emergencies?
new.x: NDMA issued the nuclear and radiological emergency guidelines in 2009.

new.s: AERB was set up in 1983 under which Act?
new.x: AERB was set up in 1983 under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962, as the independent regulator.

new.s: Which agency is the nodal technical agency for nuclear and radiological emergencies, with a Crisis Management Group?
new.x: DAE is the nodal technical agency with the Crisis Management Group; the Environmental Survey Laboratory only monitors.

new.s: In August 2019, APPCB issued a show-cause notice to UCIL over concerns linked to:
o: Seepage from the tailings pond at Tummalapalle
new.x: Villagers blamed seepage from the unlined tailings pond for uranium in groundwater; APPCB issued a show-cause notice to UCIL in Aug 2019.

new.s: According to the Centre and UCIL, high uranium in groundwater around Tummalapalle comes from:
new.x: The Centre and UCIL, citing a BARC isotope study, say the high uranium comes from the natural ore body.

new.s: India's first Dark Sky Park (2024) is located at:
new.x: Pench (Maharashtra) is India's first Dark Sky Park (2024); Hanle (2022) is the first Dark Sky Reserve.

new.s: India's first Dark Sky Reserve at Hanle lies in which protected area?
new.x: Hanle Dark Sky Reserve (2022) is in the Changthang WLS, Ladakh, chosen for clear skies, low humidity and high altitude.

new.s: Paddy husk and cattle dung belong to which category of solid waste?
new.x: Agricultural waste covers crop residues, paddy husk and cattle dung; it is biodegradable and dung becomes biogas under GOBARdhan.

new.s: Construction and demolition waste is mostly:
o: Inert material such as concrete, bricks and debris
new.x: C&D waste is mostly inert – concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris.

new.s: Of total healthcare waste, about what share is hazardous (infectious, chemical or radioactive), as per WHO?
new.x: About 85% of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous and about 15% hazardous.

new.s: Natural rubber and wool are classed as:
new.x: Wool (keratin fibre) and natural rubber are biodegradable; synthetic rubber is not.

new.s: Polythene is a polymer of:
new.x: Polythene is a polymer of ethylene (C2H4); PVC is made from vinyl chloride.

new.s: Which of the following polymers is biodegradable?
new.x: PHBV, Nylon-2-Nylon-6, PLA and PGA are biodegradable polymers; PVC, Teflon and polystyrene are not.

new.s: India generates about how much municipal solid waste a year?
new.x: India generates over 62 million tonnes of MSW a year, about 60% of it urban.

new.s: Which mega city of India generates the most solid waste per person yearly?
new.x: Delhi is the mega city with the most solid waste per person; Maharashtra is the highest-generating State.

new.s: India's first major nurdle landing in Kerala was linked to which shipwreck?
new.x: The MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck caused India's first major nurdle landing in Kerala (LDPE, HDPE).

new.s: In the waste hierarchy, using an item again in the same form is called:
new.x: Reuse means using the item again in the same form; recycling converts waste into other usable materials.

new.s: Which option is the least preferred in the waste hierarchy?
new.x: Reduction at source is the top priority; landfilling is the least preferred.

new.s: Red mud is a waste of which industry?
new.x: Red mud comes from alumina refining; steel slag from steel plants, phosphogypsum from phosphoric acid plants.

new.s: Phosphogypsum, used as a gypsum substitute and soil conditioner, comes from:
o: Phosphoric acid and phosphatic fertiliser plants
new.x: Phosphogypsum is a by-product of phosphoric acid / phosphatic fertiliser plants.

new.s: Chromium sludge is a hazardous waste mainly from:
new.x: Chromium sludge comes from tanneries.

new.s: Fly ash can partly replace which material, as noted in UPSC 2015?
new.x: Fly ash partly replaces Portland cement and is used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about steel slag:
1. It can be used as road base.
2. It can be used in agricultural soil.
3. It can be used in cement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Steel slag can be used for road base, agricultural soil and cement – all three (UPSC 2020).

new.s: Incineration reduces the volume of waste by about:
new.x: Controlled burning in oxygen at high heat cuts waste volume by about 90%.

new.s: Plasma gasification uses electricity and high heat without combustion to produce:
new.x: Plasma gasification produces syngas and can dispose of all organic wastes.

new.s: Broken glass is best disposed of by:
new.x: In the APPSC-G2 2023 match, broken glass goes to landfilling; organic waste to composting, e-waste to recycling.

new.s: Vermiculture is:
new.x: Vermiculture is the science of raising earthworms.

new.s: The Bangalore method of composting takes about how long?
new.x: The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits with alternate layers of MSW and night soil for 4–6 months.

new.s: Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) is made from:
new.x: RDF is shredded, dehydrated high-calorific MSW used as fuel in cement kilns and thermal plants.

new.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, used diapers and sanitary napkins go into which stream?
new.x: The 2026 Rules create a separate sanitary stream; under 2016 they were wrapped into the dry bin.

new.s: In the municipal waste collection chain, which step comes immediately after the Material Recovery Facility?
new.x: The chain is door-to-door, segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing/recycling, then residual landfill.

new.s: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 came into effect on:
new.x: The SWM Rules 2016 took effect from 8 April 2016 and extended beyond municipal areas.

new.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, a Bulk Waste Generator that does not treat wet waste on site must obtain:
new.x: Bulk Waste Generators must treat wet waste on site or get an EBWGR certificate.

new.s: The Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 came into force on:
new.x: The SWM Rules 2026 (under EPA 1986) are in force from 1 April 2026; 1 Oct 2025 was the draft proposal.

new.s: Under the PWM Amendment Rules, 2021, the minimum carry-bag thickness from 30 September 2021 was:
new.x: 75 microns applied from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022.

new.s: The Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 set the carry-bag thickness at:
new.x: The 2016 Rules set 50 microns; the 2011 Rules had 40 microns.

new.s: Plastic roads were promoted under which rules?
new.x: The PWM Rules 2016 brought the 50-micron limit, a PWM fee and promoted plastic roads.

new.s: How many single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022?
new.x: 19 identified single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022; the ban covers only about 11% of plastic waste.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the single-use plastic ban of 1 July 2022?
new.x: HDPE milk bottles are not banned; ear buds with plastic sticks, plastic flags and thermocol for decoration are.

new.s: EPR certificates under the plastic-packaging framework are generated by recyclers on the portal of:
new.x: On the CPCB EPR portal, recyclers generate tradable EPR certificates.

new.s: In July 2023, which country banned thin produce bags in supermarkets?
new.x: New Zealand banned thin produce bags in July 2023; Bangladesh was first to ban thin bags (2002).

new.s: Resin code 3 denotes which plastic?
new.x: Code 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others incl. polycarbonate.

new.s: Who was elected chair at INC-5.3 of the plastics treaty talks in Geneva in February 2026?
new.x: INC-5.3 (Geneva, Feb 2026) was organisational only and elected Julio Cordano as new chair.

new.s: Nurdles, the primary plastic pellets, measure:
new.x: Nurdles are primary pellets of 1–5 mm; microplastics are up to 5 mm.

new.s: How many EEE items are covered by the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022?
new.x: The 2022 Rules cover 106 EEE items, including solar PV waste.

new.s: As per the Global E-waste Monitor 2024, about what share of e-waste in 2022 was formally recycled?
new.x: GEM 2024: 62 million tonnes generated in 2022, only 22.3% formally recycled.

new.s: The Global E-waste Monitor 2024 reported global e-waste generation in 2022 of about:
new.x: 62 Mt in 2022, projected to reach 82 Mt by 2030.

new.s: About what share of e-waste in India is processed informally?
new.x: About 78% of e-waste is processed informally, in hubs like Seelampur and Moradabad.

new.s: Which e-waste constituent mainly harms the kidney and bone?
new.x: Cadmium harms kidney and bone; mercury harms brain and kidney; PBBs have endocrine effects.

new.s: Under the BMW Rules, 2016, sharps such as needles and blades go into which category?
new.x: Sharps go into White (translucent); glassware into Blue; recyclable plastics into Red.

new.s: Yellow-category biomedical waste such as anatomical waste is treated by:
o: Incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial
new.x: Yellow waste goes for incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial; Red goes for autoclave/microwave and shredding.

new.s: The tracking app for COVID-19 biomedical waste launched by CPCB is:
new.x: CPCB issued COVID-19 guidelines (2020) and the COVID19BWM tracking app.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. They replaced the 1998 Rules.
2. They introduced barcoding and GPS tracking.
3. They have not been amended since 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 2016 Rules replaced the 1998 Rules and use barcoding and GPS; they were amended in 2018 and 2019, so 3 is wrong.

new.s: India's first C&D waste recycling plant was set up at:
new.x: The first C&D waste recycling plant is at Burari (Delhi); India generates about 12 million tonnes of C&D waste a year.

new.s: The EPR framework under the C&D Waste Management Rules, 2025 applies to producers with projects of at least:
new.x: EPR applies to producers with projects of 20,000 sq m or more; recycling targets go from 25% (2025-26) to 100% (2028-29).

new.s: The LG Polymers gas leak at Visakhapatnam in May 2020 involved:
new.x: LG Polymers (May 2020) leaked styrene vapour; Bhopal (1984) involved methyl isocyanate.

new.s: The Bhopal gas tragedy of December 1984 involved which chemical?
new.x: The Union Carbide leak at Bhopal (2-3 Dec 1984) was of methyl isocyanate.

new.s: The MSIHC Rules, 1989 deal with:
o: Manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals
new.x: MSIHC Rules 1989 cover manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals; the PLI Act 1991 gives no-fault insurance.

new.s: Hazardous waste that must be landfilled is disposed of in:
new.x: Hazardous waste disposal uses secure landfills, and landfill is the last resort.

new.s: India ratified the Basel Convention in:
new.x: India ratified Basel in June 1992; it acceded to Rotterdam in 2005.

new.s: The Rotterdam Convention is concerned with:
o: Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides in trade
new.x: Rotterdam (2004) is about Prior Informed Consent; Stockholm POPs; Minamata mercury; Ramsar wetlands.

new.s: The Total Sanitation Campaign was launched in:
new.x: TSC began in 1999; CRSP 1986; Nirmal Gram Puraskar 2003; Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan 2012.

new.s: The ILCS scheme (1980-81) aimed at:
o: Converting dry latrines into pour-flush and freeing manual scavengers
new.x: ILCS converted dry latrines into pour-flush ones and freed manual scavengers.

new.s: Nirmal Gram Puraskar, introduced in 2003, was:
new.x: Nirmal Gram Puraskar (2003) was an award for ODF panchayats.

new.s: Swachh Bharat Diwas is observed on:
new.x: Swachh Bharat Diwas is 2 October; Swachhata Hi Seva is a fortnight of shramdaan held since 2017.

new.s: Swachhata Hi Seva, a fortnight of shramdaan, has been held since:
new.x: Swachhata Hi Seva has been held since 2017.

new.s: Under SBM-Urban 2.0, 'ODF++' certification adds which requirement to ODF+?
new.x: ODF++ adds safe faecal-sludge management; Water+ adds treatment of used water before discharge.

new.s: The outlay of SBM-Urban 2.0 (2021-26) is about:
new.x: SBM-U 2.0 has an outlay of ₹1.41 lakh crore and covers all statutory towns.

new.s: Under SBM-Grameen, the greywater management assistance for villages with population up to 5,000 is:
new.x: Greywater: ₹280/capita up to 5,000 population and ₹660/capita above 5,000.

new.s: Swachh Survekshan is conducted by:
new.x: Swachh Survekshan (from 2016, MoHUA) is conducted by the Quality Council of India.

new.s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, which city was the cleanest big city?
new.x: Ahmedabad was the cleanest big city; Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai were in the Super Swachh League.

new.s: Which city was ranked cleanest in the Swachh Bharat Survey 2015?
new.x: Mysore topped the 2015 survey of 476 cities; Indore was cleanest in SS 2017.

new.s: In August 2021, Andhra Pradesh became the first State with more than one:
new.x: In Aug 2021 AP became the first State with more than one Water Plus city (three).

new.s: Under CLAP, households were given a three-bin set of which colours?
new.x: CLAP gave 40 lakh households a green, blue and red 3-bin set.

new.s: The successor of CLAP, launched in January 2025, is:
new.x: Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra (Jan 2025) succeeded CLAP (Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam).

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's ban on flexi banners was deferred to take effect from:
new.x: The flexi-banner ban was announced in Aug 2022 (G.O. Ms. No. 65) and deferred to 26 January 2023.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's flexi-banner ban was announced through which order in August 2022?
new.x: The ban was announced in Aug 2022 through G.O. Ms. No. 65.

new.s: Ongole's legacy-waste biomining site, which supplies RDF to cement plants, is at:
new.x: Ongole's biomining is at Guthikondavaripalem, with RDF sent to cement plants.

new.s: Swachha Andhra Corporation (SAC) functions in Andhra Pradesh as the:
o: State agency for urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0
new.x: SAC is the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0; APEMC tracks hazardous-waste vehicles by GPS.

new.s: As per the Global Carbon Budget 2025, India's rank among fossil-CO2 emitting countries is:
new.x: China (~31.8%) leads, then the USA (~12.7%), then India (~8.3%, 3rd).

new.s: India's per capita CO2 emission is about:
o: 2 tonnes, the lowest in the G20
new.x: India emits about 2 t CO2 per capita against a world average of ~4.7 t, the lowest in the G20.

new.s: The cement sector accounts for about what share of India's GHG emissions?
new.x: Cement is about 6%, aluminium about 2.8% and waste 2.56% (2020, BUR-4).

new.s: A 'carbon bomb' is a fossil-fuel project that could emit in its lifetime more than:
new.x: Carbon bombs are projects that could emit over 1 Gt CO2; India's include Gevra and Rajmahal coal mines.

new.s: India's 2035 NDC targets what share of non-fossil power capacity?
new.x: The 2035 NDC targets 60% non-fossil power capacity and a 47% emission-intensity cut over 2005.

new.s: Emissions from a company's purchased electricity fall under:
new.x: Scope 2 is purchased electricity or heat; Scope 1 is direct; Scope 3 is the rest of the value chain.

new.s: The land and water needed to produce what we consume and absorb our waste is measured by the:
new.x: The ecological footprint measures land and water needed (APPSC-GS 2018); carbon footprint measures GHGs.

new.s: As per ISFR 2023, India's forest carbon stock is about:
new.x: ISFR 2023 put forest carbon stock at 7,285.5 Mt, up 81.5 Mt over 2021.

new.s: Which country is described as carbon-negative?
new.x: Bhutan is carbon-negative; net zero means emissions balanced by removals.

new.s: The UN-REDD programme, started in 2008, is run by:
new.x: UN-REDD (2008) is run by UNDP, FAO and UNEP.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about carbon sinks:
1. Forests, soil and oceans are natural carbon sinks.
2. Chlor-alkali plants are natural carbon sinks.
3. Carbon fertilisation accounts for about 70% of Earth's recent greening.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Forests, soil and oceans are natural sinks and CO2 fertilisation explains ~70% of recent greening; chlor-alkali plants are not sinks.

new.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes CCS from CCUS?
o: CCS uses CO2, while CCUS only stores it
Both only release CO2 to the air
CCS removes CO2 from ambient air
CCS only stores captured CO2, while CCUS uses or stores it
new.x: CCS = capture, transport and storage only; CCUS = capture, then use or store.

new.s: Spreading crushed basalt on farmland to bind CO2 as carbonate is called:
new.x: Enhanced rock weathering uses crushed silicate rock like basalt; ocean alkalinity enhancement adds lime to seawater.

new.s: Adding lime or alkaline minerals to seawater to remove CO2 is known as:
new.x: Ocean alkalinity enhancement adds lime or alkaline minerals to seawater.

new.s: NET Power's Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant is located at:
new.x: NET Power's plant is at La Porte, Texas; it burns gas in oxygen with supercritical CO2 as working fluid.

new.s: How many steps does the CCS process involve?
o: Four – capture, use, transport and release
new.x: CCS has three steps: capture at a stationary point source, transport and storage.

new.s: The OCO-2 CO2-observing satellite belongs to:
new.x: OCO-2 is NASA's; GOSAT is Japan's.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a goal of the National Carbon Project?
o: Assess carbon pools of India's terrestrial biomes
Develop space technology for carbon sequestration
new.x: NCP assesses carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance; space technology for sequestration is not its goal.

new.s: One carbon credit represents:
new.x: One carbon credit equals one tonne of CO2e avoided or removed.

new.s: The Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) is run by:
new.x: VCS is run by Verra; Gold Standard was founded by WWF.

new.s: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified under which provision?
new.x: CCTS (June 2023) was notified under Sec. 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act 2001, not the EP Act.

new.s: Which body runs India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
new.x: The CCTS is run by BEE and trades Indian Carbon Credits; it is India's first mandatory compliance market.

new.s: Carbon credit prices are determined by:
new.x: Credit prices are market-set by supply and demand, not fixed by UNEP or any international body.

new.s: The EU CBAM aims to prevent:
new.x: CBAM levies carbon on imports to stop carbon leakage, i.e. emissions moving abroad.

new.s: From which year will Denmark levy its livestock carbon tax?
new.x: New Zealand proposed a livestock tax first; Denmark is the first to levy one, from 2030.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the EU CBAM?
new.x: CBAM covers iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity; textiles are not listed.

new.s: India's first Level 5 net-zero airport (2024) is:
new.x: Delhi airport became India's first Level 5 net-zero airport in 2024; Cochin is the world's first fully solar-powered airport.

new.s: The world's first fully solar-powered airport (2015) is:
new.x: Cochin airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015.

new.s: Maruti Suzuki's Gujarat rail siding is the world's first modal-shift project registered with:
new.x: It is the world's first modal-shift project under Verra's VCS.
